rationale: The archive already contains two highly correlated estimators of exactly this "policy shift" object at the same valuation conditioning — the 5-year OLS trend (alpha 0.038, t 3.76) and current-level-minus-5yr-MA (alpha 0.036, t 3.27) — so a three-year-versus-lagged-three-year average difference is a third smoothing of the same construct and is very likely to be a cosmetic estimator variant rather than new economic information.

The positive/negative-part decomposition is correctly constructed (ADD(x,ABS(x)) isolates improvers weighted by cheapness, SUB(x,ABS(x)) isolates deteriorators weighted by richness) and the expected positive sign follows, but the identical decomposition applied to payout levels already underperformed the simple conditional version (alpha 0.010, t 1.12), so the prior that the short-leg re-weighting helps is weak.

Combining the two orthogonalizations that each independently improved alpha (within-firm valuation ranking and the trend-measured financing leg) is a coherent test of whether they compound or overlap, though there is a real risk that TS_RANK of the EV multiple mostly picks up the same firm-specific state that a rising payout trend already encodes, making the two legs mechanically correlated.

A clean single-component ablation of the winning signal with a pre-stated interpretive fork in either direction, which is legitimate mechanism testing even if it is low-ambition and its most likely outcome is a modest degradation that merely confirms the debt leg contributes.

target_name: Noise Scaled Payout Trajectory When Cheap
rationale: Dividing a 5-year slope by the 5-year volatility of the same series is numerically unstable — firms with near-zero financing variability (many of them precisely the inactive, uninformative ones) produce explosive ratios that WINSOR at 1% will not adequately tame, and the numerator is itself a component of the denominator, so the ranking risks being driven by degenerate low-dispersion cases rather than by genuine policy conviction.

Purging the profitability cycle from the trajectory directly addresses the legitimate concern that this family is an RMW-spanned recovery bet, but the two raw slopes are differenced without standardization and EBITDA/assets trends are typically far larger in magnitude than net-payout/assets trends, so the composite may end up ranking primarily on declining profitability rather than on discretionary payout expansion.
